issues.legal_issue: A decision on the merits in a contested constitutional writ proceeding can bar a later regular suit between the same parties on the same matter under the general principles of res judicata.
material_facts: The claimant sought relief in a writ petition on the ground that the State’s conduct in allowing contractors to dispose of attached goods had discharged his liability as their surety.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition on the merits after hearing the parties and rejecting the contention that the claimant had been discharged from liability.
The claimant later brought a suit against the State seeking relief on the same ground, and the same question of discharge from liability was directly in issue.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s decision on the merits in the writ petition operated as res judicata in the subsequent suit, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is not exhaustive of the application of res judicata to decisions in earlier proceedings. Under the general principle, grounded in public policy and finality of decisions, a matter decided after full contest or a fair opportunity to prove the parties’ cases by a competent court binds the same parties in a later regular suit concerning the same matter, even if the earlier proceeding was not a suit and the earlier court could not try the later suit. The court relied on Daryao v. State of U.P., Pandit M.S.M. Sharma v. Dr. Shree Krishna Sinha, and earlier authorities including Hook v. Administrator-General of Bengal, Ramachandra Rao v. Ramachandra Rao, and Mst. Bhagwati v. Mst. Ram Kali.

rule.if: prior_writ_proceeding and later_regular_suit and same_parties and same_matter and prior_decision_on_merits and fair_opportunity_to_contest

predicates.prior_writ_proceeding: The earlier proceeding was a constitutional writ proceeding between the parties.
predicates.later_regular_suit: A party later brought a regular suit concerning a matter addressed in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.same_parties: The parties to the later suit were the same parties as in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.same_matter: The same matter was directly in issue in both proceedings.
predicates.prior_decision_on_merits: The earlier court decided the matter on its merits.
predicates.fair_opportunity_to_contest: The parties had a full contest or a fair opportunity to present their cases in the earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: When a regular suit between the same parties concerns the same matter decided on its merits after a fair opportunity to contest in an earlier writ proceeding, the earlier decision bars the later suit on that matter.

issues.legal_issue: The rule barring a later claim for a portion omitted from an earlier claim in a suit does not apply to the contents of a constitutional writ petition or to a later suit because of an omission from that petition.
material_facts: The claimant argued that treating the decision in his writ petition as res judicata could also bar a later suit concerning a portion of a claim omitted from the writ petition.
The earlier proceeding was a writ petition, followed by a regular suit.
issues.conclusion: The provisions governing omission or relinquishment of part of a claim in a suit do not apply to the contents of a writ petition and therefore do not bar a subsequent suit on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Order 2, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies by its terms to suits: it requires a suit to include the whole claim arising from its cause of action and bars a later suit for a portion omitted or relinquished. Those provisions do not govern the contents of a writ petition. The court referred to Devendra Pratap Narain Rai Sharma v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

predicates.prior_writ_proceeding: A party first pursued relief in a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.later_regular_suit: A party later brought a regular suit concerning a claim related to the writ proceeding.
predicates.claim_portion_omitted_from_writ: A portion of the claim later raised in the suit was omitted from the earlier writ petition.

issues.definition: When a party later brings a regular suit after omitting a portion of the claim from an earlier writ petition, that omission does not itself bar the later suit.
